title: Jump Game II
summary: Each value says how far you may jump from that index. Find the fewest jumps that reach the last index.

tests.explain: Jump 1 step to index 1, then 4 steps from index 1 to the last index. One jump can't do it: from index 0 you reach index 2 at most.
Every value is 1, so you must step on every index: 3 jumps.
You already stand on the last index.

hints: Think in rounds, like breadth-first search: after 1 jump you can stand anywhere in some range of indices, after 2 jumps in a further range, and so on.
While scanning the indices reachable with the current number of jumps, track the furthest index any of them can reach. That becomes the end of the next round.
Keep end (the edge of the current round) and farthest. For i from 0 to n - 2: farthest = max(farthest, i + nums[i]); when i reaches end, count a jump and set end = farthest.
